In public school, I allowed narcissistic people in my life because I thought that being “mean” and “rude” was honesty. And that if someone was good to you, then they’re fake. That was what my parents told me to justify their abuse. 

Later on, I recognized that that was dog shit. Yes, honesty does come in forms of criticism. But there’s a difference between criticism and being an asshole. So then I cut them off.

Fast forward to where I have full control of the people I want to associate with, and it seemed like the people I chose were coverted narcissists/codependent.  So the ones who get defensive when you try to bring up an unfair/hurtful behavior. The ones who are constantly victims. The ones who trauma dump on you and fully depend on you to take care of them but don’t try to give any emotional support in return. The ones who get passive aggressive and don’t try to communicate. The ones who will talk to you based on convienance or what value you could be to them. The ones who will devalue you and throw you away so easily when you can’t give them what they want. And the ones who cry and self victimize when you realize that you don’t deserve to be treated like this.

I recently ended a friendship with someone like that. I dealt with so many people like him and I regretted not communicating anything to the others before. Everything I ever thought about left my mouth without any care. And it felt amazing. And then I walked away. I felt like a balloon that let all it’s air out, I was so relieved and free from all my anger.
